thread: Follow matter from individual elements into molecules that join and transform, then step into the laboratories where people explore them. The swarm can become a reactive metal, a folded molecular machine, or a curious piece of glassware.

candidates.name: Chemguide
candidates.why: Element groups, chemical bonds, transition-metal colors and organic reactions offer a cast of atoms that join, separate and change character.

candidates.name: PDB-101
candidates.why: Illustrated molecules include enzymes, molecular motors and light-catching proteins, with intricate folds and moving parts that suggest whole families of creatures.

candidates.name: Science History Institute
candidates.why: Its collections and exhibitions bring chemistry into the laboratory through alchemical imagery, historical apparatus, dyes and other material discoveries.

candidates.name: Chemistry LibreTexts
candidates.why: Open chemistry books range from atomic structure and inorganic compounds to reactions, molecular shapes and experimental techniques.

candidates.name: Chemistry Explained
candidates.why: An alphabetical chemistry encyclopedia links elements with compounds, bonds, polymers and the reactions that give materials their properties.

candidates.name: American Chemical Society
candidates.why: Its education and history sections explore chemical elements, notable discoveries, molecular structures and hands-on demonstrations.

candidates.name: Italian Chemical Society
candidates.why: Its chemistry museum and historical instrument resources introduce old laboratory apparatus, samples and analytical devices.

candidates.name: National Informal STEM Education Network
candidates.why: Hands-on chemistry and nanoscale science activities turn molecular structures, surprising materials and changes in matter into things to explore.
